independent_load_screen.revision: Rev R1.2 corrected pressure screen and reinforced heel-core roof
independent_load_screen.load_case: Conservative single-support sensitivity: entire 66 kg gravitational load assigned to one shoe; multipliers are analyst-selected sensitivities, not measured gait loads.
independent_load_screen.roof_strip_formula: sigma = 3*F*L/(2*b*h^2), L=23 mm, h=10.1 mm revised heel-core roof, b=20/30/40/60 mm assumed
independent_load_screen.pin_formula: sigma = 32*(F*span/4)/(pi*d^3), d=7.6 mm, span=40.6 and 90.3 mm sensitivity only
limitations: The old pressure screen incorrectly used the full 55 x 23 mm cavity area as bladder area; this correction uses the specified 27 x 22 mm target bladder body footprint (594 mm2). Actual pressure-effective area may be smaller.

The 0.40 MPa working / 0.50 MPa nominal relief settings are provisional design targets only. They are not approved until the finished bladder has an OEM-declared working/burst/cycle rating, the AP20-D flow/overshoot is checked, and measured chamber pressure transients stay below all component ratings.

At the provisional 0.50 MPa relief target, nominal bladder support is only 297 N at the assumed full projected area. The chassis/structural load path must safely carry the residual and must withstand the full load with the bladder depressurized; this is not demonstrated by the current strip screen.
The Lee Spring candidate is a 20.5–30.8 N return spring at an assumed 4–6 mm compression and is not a body-load spring.
No finite-element solver/workflow was available or run. Roof-strip and pin-beam analyses are analyst-defined sensitivity models, not validated stress/load-path analyses or design allowables.
Candidate material reference values do not account for manufacturing direction, notches, contact, fatigue or impact. No physical tests or human wear tests were performed.
